traditions/syro-malabar-catholic/summary: The majority of the St Thomas Christians of Kerala, who trace their faith to the apostle Thomas and inherited the East Syriac liturgy from the Church of the East. Latinised under Portuguese rule after the Synod of Diamper (1599), the community split after the Coonan Cross Oath (1653); those who stayed with Rome became the Syro-Malabar Church. It received its own Indian hierarchy in 1923 and major archiepiscopal status in 1992, and is notable for numerous priestly and religious vocations serving worldwide.
traditions/syro-malabar-catholic/distinc: East Syriac liturgical heritage of the St Thomas Christians
Very high number of priests and religious
Major Archbishop in Ernakulam (Raphael Thattil since 2024)
Internal dispute since the 1990s over how the Qurbana is celebrated (facing the people or the altar)
traditions/syro-malabar-catholic/profile: Scripture and Tradition interpreted by the magisterium of the Pope and bishops, together with the church's own patristic and liturgical heritage.
Salvation by grace through Christ, received in faith and the sacraments; Eastern Catholics often express this, like the Orthodox, as deification (theosis).
Seven sacraments; the Holy Qurbana in the East Syriac tradition (Anaphora of Addai and Mari), with retained Latin influences.
Catholic teaching on resurrection, judgement, heaven and hell, with prayer for the departed; Eastern Catholics often describe purification after death in Eastern rather than Latin terms.
Major Archbishop of Ernakulam-Angamaly with the Synod of Bishops, governed as a church sui iuris under the Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches (1990), in full communion with the Bishop of Rome.
Holy Qurbana in Malayalam and Syriac; distinctive St Thomas Christian customs (e.g. the 'Mar Thoma Sleeva' cross).
traditions/syro-malabar-catholic/status: Active; c. 4.25 million faithful (2017), the second-largest Eastern Catholic church.
traditions/syro-malankara-catholic/summa: A church of Kerala formed when Archbishop Geevarghese Mar Ivanios, founder of the Bethany monastic order, and Bishop Jacob Mar Theophilos of the Malankara Orthodox Church entered Catholic communion in 1930, keeping the West Syriac (Antiochene) liturgy. It became a major archiepiscopal church in 2005.

Reunion movement led by Mar Ivanios (1930)
Seat at Thiruvananthapuram; Major Archbishop Baselios Cleemis since 2007

traditions/coptic-catholic/summary: The Alexandrian-rite church in communion with Rome. Its organised history begins in 1741, when the Coptic bishop Amba Athanasius of Jerusalem became Catholic and Rome created a vicariate for Catholic Copts; the patriarchate was effectively established by Leo XIII in 1895. It runs a substantial network of schools and social services in Upper Egypt.
traditions/coptic-catholic/distinctives/: Coptic (Alexandrian) liturgy in Coptic and Arabic
Patriarch of Alexandria resident in Cairo
Schools and social work especially in Upper Egypt

traditions/ethiopian-eritrean-catholic/n: Ethiopian and Eritrean Catholic Churches (Ge'ez rite)
traditions/ethiopian-eritrean-catholic/s: The Ge'ez-rite Catholic churches of Ethiopia and Eritrea. After the failed Jesuit-led union of the 17th century, a lasting Catholic community grew from the mission of St Justin de Jacobis (from 1839). An ordinariate for Ge'ez-rite Catholics was created in 1930, a metropolitan church sui iuris in Addis Ababa in 1961, and a separate Eritrean Catholic Church sui iuris in 2015.

traditions/ethiopian-eritrean-catholic/s: Active; small minorities in both countries.
traditions/armenian-catholic/summary: The Armenian-rite church in communion with Rome, constituted when Pope Benedict XIV confirmed Abraham Petros I Ardzivian as Patriarch of Cilicia of the Armenians in 1742. The Mekhitarist monks of San Lazzaro in Venice (from 1717) made it a centre of Armenian scholarship. Devastated by the 1915 genocide, the patriarchate has resided in Beirut since 1928.

Martyrdom in 1915 (e.g. Bishop Ignatius Maloyan, beatified 2001 and canonised 2025)

traditions/syriac-catholic/summary: The West Syriac church in communion with Rome. A Catholic patriarch, Andrew Akhijan, was installed in Aleppo in 1662, but the line lapsed in 1702; it was renewed in 1782–83 by Michael Jarweh, who had been elected Syriac Orthodox patriarch and declared himself Catholic, establishing the patriarchal monastery of Sharfeh in Lebanon. Its patriarch resides in Beirut; its Iraqi communities (Qaraqosh/Bakhdida) suffered displacement by the Islamic State in 2014.

traditions/ruthenian-catholic/summary: The Byzantine-rite Catholic church of the Carpatho-Rusyn people, founded at the Union of Uzhhorod (1646). Its Mukachevo eparchy in Transcarpathia was liquidated by the Soviets in 1949 and restored in 1989. Immigrants brought it to the United States, where disputes with Latin bishops over married priests led many to join Orthodoxy (from 1891), while the remainder became the Byzantine Catholic Metropolitan Church of Pittsburgh.

traditions/polish-national-catholic/summ: A church founded among Polish immigrants in Scranton, Pennsylvania, in 1897 under Fr (later Bishop) Francis Hodur, after disputes with the Roman Catholic hierarchy over parish property and Polish leadership. Hodur received episcopal consecration from Old Catholic bishops at Utrecht in 1907. The church belonged to the Union of Utrecht until 2003, when it withdrew over the ordination of women and related changes in other Old Catholic churches.
traditions/polish-national-catholic/dist: Lay ownership and control of parish property
Vernacular (Polish, later English) Mass from the early twentieth century
Proclamation of the Word of God, heard and preached, counted as a sacrament
Ongoing dialogue with the Roman Catholic Church
traditions/polish-national-catholic/prof: Scripture and Tradition as received in the undivided church of the first millennium; no recognition of papal infallibility or universal jurisdiction.
Salvation by God's grace through Christ received in faith and the sacraments.
Seven sacraments, with the Word of God additionally treated as a sacrament; general (public) confession for adults alongside private confession.
Catholic hope of resurrection and eternal life; Hodur's teaching that all may ultimately reach salvation has been influential.
Bishops with a Prime Bishop and General Synods including clergy and laity.
